basis: Beta2-microglobulin amyloid damages joints, bones and tendons; carpal tunnel neuropathy is common (>30%); antecedent renal failure is excluded.
Symptomatic abnormal positioning of the colon; proximity to the liver and diaphragm does not establish injury to those organs.
Inherited retinal dystrophy caused by dominant IMPG1 variants.
Benign female reproductive system adenofibroma; its site lies outside the organ axes.
Usually bacterial infection causing purulent inflammation of lymph nodes; no blood-cell or marrow disease is established.
Neurological syndrome defined by deficient cerebral folate availability or metabolism, with normal peripheral folate metabolism.
Well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor of the endocrine pancreas; exocrine pancreatic injury is not established.
Severe syndromic intellectual disability with hypotonia; seizures occur in 35%. Other structural organ findings have unspecified frequencies.
Primary immune deficiency; bronchiectasis documents chronic airway damage in 12/16 patients (75%). Organ enlargement and gut nodules alone do not establish dysfunction.
Defined by malignant tumor occupying the eye; the primary cancer's site is unspecified.
Hormone-producing neoplasm arising in the pituitary gland; effects on additional organs vary by secreted hormone and tumor size.
Hereditary cerebellar neurodegeneration; damaging retinal or optic nerve involvement is restricted to particular subtypes.
Retinopathy, obesity/hypogonadism and polydactyly define the phenotype; renal abnormalities are a major BBS criterion. Subtype-specific frequencies are unavailable.
Balantidium infection of the large intestine causes colitis and dysentery.
Beckwith-Wiedemann phenotype includes cardinal macroglossia/abdominal wall defects and hyperinsulinism. Organ enlargement and future tumor risk do not establish damage.
Primary skeletal dysplasia affecting femoral epiphyses, femoral necks, hips and other skeletal sites.
Glycerol metabolism defect causing pseudohypertriglyceridemia in otherwise healthy adults; no additional organ damage is established.
Generalized epilepsy syndrome. Nonspecific mouth findings and eye movement abnormalities do not establish gastrointestinal or ocular tissue damage.
Autoimmune destruction of adrenal cortex. Pigmentation, hypotension, weakness and digestive symptoms do not establish direct damage to additional organs.
Inherited skin and hair pigment anomaly; reported nystagmus and photophobia lack documented frequency or evidence of damaging ocular involvement.
Malignant Paget cells infiltrate skin, including genital or perianal skin; associated internal cancers are separate diseases.
Congenital isolated growth hormone deficiency; short stature and delayed maturation do not establish intrinsic skeletal damage.
Immune dysregulation with common autoimmune cytopenias; intrinsic inflammatory enteropathy occurs in roughly 50-60%. Bronchiectasis is below 30%.
Tumor arises from parasympathetic aortic-body paraganglia, not the aortic wall; proximity to heart and vessels does not establish cardiovascular damage.
Genetic neonatal diabetes reflecting endocrine pancreatic dysfunction; remission and later recurrence do not establish additional organ damage.
